lines.t: I was so sure that I knew You then,
Behind stained glass, wrought by human might.
I called the men who held the door "Your hands,"
Then watched them lock it softly from Your light.
We made slogans of Your holy name
We wore guilt, but wanted others to blame.
I leaned my weight upon a cracked reed staff
And felt the splinter pierce beneath my skin.
Shattered stained glass cold against bare feet,
A jagged color where the frost crept in.
A gap grew wide. I didn't know Your hand,
Still grasping in vain at shifting sand.
The midnight cry warned us in kindness
But I was too proud when the hour came.
You listened for the first stitch of sorrow.
To close the gap and take away my shame.
I recognize them now
That I know what to look for.
The kiss of Your words on their lips,
Your salt in the tears of their eyes,
Your care in the touch of correction,
Your shalom in the calm of Sabbath.
I cherish the You I see
In those You sent me.
True servants knelt beside the broken floor,
No polished speech nor sermons grand.
Just quiet hands that swept the path once more
Empty vessels without the doctrines of man.
With pure water they poured and quenched my thirst.
An example of simply putting You first.
I recognize them now
That I know what to look for.
The kiss of Your words on their lips,
Your salt in the tears of their eyes,
Your care in the touch of correction,
Your shalom in the calm of Sabbath.
I cherish the You I see
In those You sent me
Washed feet on hallowed ground. No walls remain,
Just grace, Your covering against the rain.
You were never the blade, nor the cold stone;
You were in the hands that swept the way back home.
I recognize them now
That I know what to look for
The kiss of Your words on their lips,
Your salt in the tears of their eyes,
Your care in the touch of correction,
Your shalom in the calm of Sabbath.
I cherish the You I see
In those You sent me.
Words seasoned with salt.
and flavored with honey.
I know the difference now.
Remade by You.
Vessels of honor.
I cherish the You I see
In those You send.
